sentences.text:
Honourable Sri Justice C.V. Bhaskar Reddy
 Writ Petition No. 3754 Of 2023
Order:

The petitioner claims to be one of the member of Indian National Congress and she was deputed to campaign in the Municipal Elections held in the year 2020 as a party worker as per the decision of the political party and as such she went to Narayanapet.

While campaigning at Narayanpet Region,
she came into contact with the 5th respondent, who claimed to be the President of the Congress Committee of Narayanapet District.

Taking advantage of the petitioner's close contact and she being a widow and living lonely, the 5th respondent by making false promise of marrying her, had sexual relationship with her and took certain photographs and started threatening her stating that if she does not agree his proposal to have sexual relationship, he will release the photos to the media.

On the said allegation the petitioner lodged a complaint before the 4th respondent, who, after verifying the said complaint, has registered a case in Crime No.209/2022 for the offences under Sections 417,
420, 376 & 506 IPC.

The grievance of the petitioner is that even after registering the crime against the 5th respondent,
the respondent police are not conducting proper investigation and filing charge sheet.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that during the pendency of the writ petition, the respondent police filed charge sheet on 06.04.2023, but they have not conducted the investigation fairly, and, in fact, with an intention to help the accused/5th respondent, they have not collected the evidence properly and the objections raised on the charge sheet.

Learned counsel further submitted that the petitioner has also filed protest petition on the file of the learned XIV Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Nampally, and during the pendency of the said petition she also filed I.A.No.02 of 2023 to change the Investigating Officer and to conduct proper and fresh investigation into the said crime.

entities.text: XIV Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Nampally
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home appearing for the respondent police has submitted that basing on the material evidence, the respondent police after conducting proper investigation had already filed charge sheet before the Magistrate concerned and if the petitioner is having any grievance on the charge sheet, she is entitled to file appropriate application before the Magistrate concerned.

As per section 173(8) Cr.P.C., the Investigating Officer is not precluded to conduct further investigation in respect of an offence after a report under sub-section (2) has been forwarded to the Magistrate and, whereupon such investigation, the officer in-charge of the police station obtains further evidence, oral or documentary, he shall forward to the Magistrate a further report or reports regarding such evidence in the form prescribed and the provisions of sub-sections (2) to (6) shall, as Smt. A.Sreelatha vs The State Of Telangana And 4 Others on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10753734/
1 far as may be, apply in relation to such report or reports as they apply in relation to a report forwarded under sub-section (2).

entities.text: Smt. A.Sreelatha vs The State Of Telangana And 4 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the said provision, if the petitioner is having any material, oral or documentary, in support of her grievance that the respondent police have not conducted fair and proper investigation, she is entitled to produce such evidence to enable the Investigating Officer to exercise his powers as conferred under Section 173(8) Cr.P.C.
In addition to the said provision, under Section 216 Cr.P.C., power has been conferred on the Court to alter or add any charge at any time before the judgment is pronounced.
In Anant Prakash Sinha vs State of Haryana1, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that court can change or alter the charge if there is a defect or something is left out.

entities.text: Anant Prakash Sinha vs State of Haryana1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above, the petitioner is having alternative remedy of either approaching the police by making appropriate representation duly enclosing additional evidence, oral or documentary, for conducting investigation and also filing additional report or filing an application before the Magistrate concerned to alter or add (2016) 2 SCJ 735 any of the charge at any time of the trial, if she feels that there is a defect in laying of the charge sheet.

Therefore, this Court deems it appropriate to relegate the petitioner to avail the remedies available to her in accordance with law for redressal of her grievance either by making an application before the police concerned or filing an appropriate complaint before the court concerned that something is left out in the charge sheet and investigation has not been properly done.
With the above liberty, the writ petition is disposed of.
No order as to costs.
Miscellaneous applications, pending if any, shall stand closed.

C.V. BHASKAR REDDY, J Date: 20.07.2023 ES/KTM Smt. A.Sreelatha vs The State Of Telangana And 4 Others on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10753734/
2
